R6I-bear-backcountry-0001.name: By Blackstock Creek
R6I-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R6I-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Burn from 2018 (fire R41945), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 22 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Blackstock Creek 100 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.1 km and about 1 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
